name: THE MINE: THE LINE
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE ORE CART
LOOK_AT: An ore cart on its side, one wheel in the air.
Empty. Whoever pushed it this far gave up at the same junction I'm standing at.
There's a name chalked on it: MAY. A woman or a month. Either way, she's gone.
LISTEN_TO: The wheel ticking round when I touch it, slower, then stopped.
Quiet. It's been waiting a long while for somebody to make up their mind.
A drip into its bed, where the rust has made a little cup.

overrides.PUSH: I tried to set it on its wheels. It went back on its side, where it's comfortable.
overrides.TALK_TO: I asked May which way she went. She kept it to herself. I'd want the same, if I were May.
overrides.USE: I could climb in and go somewhere. It's on its side, and I'm a grown man. Two good reasons.

subjects.name: THE LEFT PASSAGE
LOOK_AT: A passage into the dark, timbered, the width of a man and a half.
Exactly like the other one. I've checked twice.
I counted the timbers. Seven. I'm not going to count the other side.
LISTEN_TO: Still air, and a drip. Nothing to choose by.

subjects.name: THE RIGHT PASSAGE
LOOK_AT: A passage into the dark, timbered, the same width as its neighbor.
I've compared the two. They're the same passage, as far as I can tell, in two places.
I counted the timbers. I'd told myself I wouldn't. Seven.
LISTEN_TO: A drip, somewhere down it, at much the same pace.
Still air. It isn't telling either.
Still air, and a drip. Nothing to choose by either.

subjects.name: THE WAY BACK
LOOK_AT: I could go back and apologize to the small rock. I won't, but I could.
Back to the rocks. The small one will be pleased to see me.
LISTEN_TO: A trickle of grit, back toward the rocks.
Quiet, back there, and getting no louder.
A drip, back there, keeping time.
